chunks: Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: There is no harm with the pleasant scent between As-Safa and Al-Marwah from the scent of the perfumers, and one does not need to hold one's nose, so it does not contradict the report of Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said in it: One holds one's nose from the pleasant scent for two reasons: one is that the command to hold the nose is directed only at the one who is directly engaging in the act with his own self, so it is appropriate for him to hold his nose; but if he is passing by on a path and the scent reaches him, then it is not obligatory upon him to do so. The other aspect is that we consider the command to hold the nose to be a type of recommendation (istihbab), and this is upon permissibility.

key_terms.الاستِحباب: Recommendation (a legal status less than obligation but more than mere permissibility)
key_terms.الصّفا: As-Safa (one of the two hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.المروة: Al-Marwah (the second hill in the Sa'i ritual)
key_terms.خَبَرَ مُعَاوِيَةَ بنِ عَمّارٍ: The report of Muawiya ibn Ammar

ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory to hold one's nose while passing perfumers during Hajj or Umrah Sa'i?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on pleasant scents during the Sa'i, distinguishing between those who apply perfume themselves and those merely passing by. He resolves the apparent contradiction with Muawiya ibn 'Ammar's report by interpreting the instruction to hold one's nose as either specific to the wearer or merely recommended (mustahabb) rather than obligatory, thereby easing the burden on pilgrims in public spaces. This reflects the Shia scholarly principle of reconciling narrations through contextual interpretation (ta'wil) and distinguishing between strict obligation (wujub) and recommendation (istihbab).
